title: Cohomology bounds descend from finite local models
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R=\Gamma(*)$ and $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] for schemes $T$. Let $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_S))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\{V_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ is a finite covering family of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Fix integers $r\le s$ and scalar cochain complexes $Q_i^\bullet$ with $Q_i^q=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$. Assume $Q|_{V_i}\simeq\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R Q_i^\bullet$ in the derived category, where scalar modules mean constant sheaves as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Assume each functor $M\mapsto\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R M$ on $R$-modules is exact and every $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Then $H^q(Q)=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$, and
$$H^q(Q)|_{V_i}\simeq\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R H^q(Q_i^\bullet).$$
In particular each $H^q(Q)$ has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] and is constructible on the single stratum $S$, so $Q\in\Dbc(S,\Gamma)$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-localization-exact-cohomology] to each $u_i:V_i\to S$. It identifies the given restriction with exact sectionwise module restriction, with the canonical coefficient action, and gives $H^q(Q)|_{V_i}\cong H^q(Q|_{V_i})$.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; condensed ringed-module cohomology specialization isolated in the cited child.

proof.text: Set $E_i(M)=\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_{R_{V_i}}M_{V_i}$, with constant sheaves as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. This is the assumed exact functor. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^q(E_i(Q_i^\bullet))\cong E_i(H^q(Q_i^\bullet))$. Apply the derived cohomology functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the given model isomorphism and compose with Step 1. This proves the required isomorphism on each original $V_i$, without asserting flatness of arbitrary coefficients.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; exact-functor cohomology and derived cohomology functoriality.

proof.text: For $q\notin[r,s]$, $Q_i^q=0$, hence $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)=\ker d_i^q/\operatorname{im}d_i^{q-1}=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Exact additive $E_i$ preserves zero, so Step 2 gives $H^q(Q)|_{V_i}=0$.

Write $F=H^q(Q)$ for such $q$. Every test object $W$ has the base-changed cover $\{W\times_SV_i\to W\}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. By Step 3 and sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $F(W\times_SV_i)=0$. Every section of $F(W)$ therefore agrees locally with zero; uniqueness in the sheaf equalizer axiom gives $F(W)=0$, hence $F=0$. For an empty covering that same axiom makes $F(W)$ a singleton.

source.place: Tags 00VH, definition-site (base change), and 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets (uniqueness, including the empty cover).

proof.text: The finitely presented $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)$ and Step 2 witness finite constant local models [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The identity immersion is a one-piece stratification [def-constructible-stratification]: $S=S\cap(S\setminus\varnothing)$ is constructible since $S,\varnothing$ are open retrocompact [def-weil-constructible-subset]. For the affine-local convention without quasi-separatedness, take the equivalent scalar-matrix cokernel presentations in the local-model node and restrict to the base-changed cover of each affine open. Exact restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] preserves their cokernels and finite sums; coefficient restriction preserves multiplication and the same scalar entries [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization]. These presentations give finite constant local models there too. Clause (1) of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] gives constructibility. The finite interval proved in Step 4 and clause (2) give $Q\in\Dbc(S,\Gamma)$.
